profile.name: Thippeswamy K.S.
profile.eyebrow: Computer Vision · Machine Learning · Robotics Perception
profile.headline: I build perception systems that let vehicles and robots understand where they are and what is around them.
profile.summary: Computer Vision & ML engineer working on detection, segmentation, tracking, monocular depth, visual odometry and SLAM on real sensor data: camera, LiDAR, IMU and GPS. I take models from data and labeling, through training and evaluation, to real-time deployment with PyTorch, TensorRT, C++ and ROS 2. Author of an IEEE DISCOVER 2026 paper on vision-based odometry.
profile.looking_for: Computer Vision, Machine Learning and robotics-perception roles

parts.title: Computer Vision & Machine Learning
parts.intro: Perception models trained on real data, evaluated against ground truth and run in real time. This is the work I want to keep doing.

featured.short: Dashcam + phone GPS → road-sign map checked against OpenStreetMap. C++, live at 10 Hz on a laptop GPU, 3.2 m median ATE over 33 KITTI / nuScenes / Oxford drives.
featured.title: InfraStructer: Road-Infrastructure Audit from a Single Camera
featured.tagline: Turns dashcam or phone footage plus phone GPS into a map of road signs, checked against OpenStreetMap, with no LiDAR and no RTK.
bullets: An end-to-end perception pipeline: object and traffic-sign detection → multi-object tracking with appearance re-identification → monocular metric depth → visual odometry → OpenStreetMap map matching → landmark map.
Rewrote the original ROS 2 / Python prototype as a C++ pipeline (v2.0). It runs live at 10 Hz on a single laptop GPU without dropping frames.

Deployed models as TorchScript, ONNX and TensorRT FP16 engines: YOLOv8 sign detectors trained on GTSDB and CCTSDB2021, and Depth Anything 3 metric depth. Pose graph and trajectory correction use GTSAM.
Every code change runs a regression benchmark on 33 real drives from KITTI, Oxford RobotCar and nuScenes. Each run is stored as a baseline so the next change can be compared against it, run by run.

metrics.label: median trajectory error (ATE), camera + start/end GPS fixes only

featured.short: SAM2 + CoTracker3 auto-labeling: annotate one frame, export YOLO detection, segmentation and pose datasets for the whole video. On PyPI.

media.alt: AutoSegmentor propagating instance masks for road, vehicles and riders across an Indian street video
media.caption: Masks for road, vehicles and riders propagated across a street video from a few clicks.

featured.title: AutoSegmentor: Video-to-Dataset Auto-Labeling
featured.tagline: Annotate one frame and get detection, segmentation and pose labels for the whole video.
bullets: Combines SAM2 mask propagation with CoTracker3 keypoint tracking. Clicks or boxes on one frame carry masks and keypoints across long, complex videos.
A single export produces YOLO datasets for object detection, instance segmentation and pose estimation at the same time, with built-in augmentation and dataset versioning.
Generates semi-synthetic training data from real footage using the exact masks, so models train robustly from very little hand-labeled data.
A PyQt5 desktop app with multi-class point and box annotation, a precision zoom and an async GPU engine that keeps the UI responsive. Released as a pip package with a documentation site.

featured.short: YOLOv8-Seg drivable-region and object perception for Indian roads, trained on a 45,000+ image dataset I built from 40 videos.

media.alt: YOLOv8-Seg road segmentation predictions on a validation batch, including noisy and low-light augmented frames
media.caption: Validation predictions from the road-segmentation model, including augmented noisy frames.

featured.title: Drivable-Region & Object Perception for Indian Roads
featured.tagline: Road segmentation and object detection for unstructured Indian traffic, built during my MURTI research internship.
bullets: Trained YOLOv8-Seg for road and drivable-space segmentation, object detection and instance segmentation, so the vehicle knows where it can travel.
Built a dataset of 45,000+ annotated images from 40 videos of Indian roads, covering different weather, lighting and road types.
Refined road masks with SLIC superpixels and tuned inference for real-time use at 854×480.

parts.title: Robotics, SLAM & Localization
parts.intro: Knowing where the vehicle is, and placing what the camera sees in 3D: visual odometry, SLAM, sensor fusion and ROS 2.

featured.short: Five monocular VO methods (feature, optical-flow, deep) compared on KITTI and a new campus dataset, on a Jetson Xavier NX. IEEE DISCOVER 2026.
featured.title: Visual Odometry Benchmark for Low-Compute Vehicles
featured.tagline: How well do feature-based, optical-flow and deep-learning visual odometry methods work on an embedded computer, outside the benchmark?
bullets: Compared five monocular VO approaches (feature-based, optical-flow-based and deep-learning-based) on KITTI and on a new campus-scale GITAM dataset. The dataset was recorded on an autonomous ground vehicle with camera, LiDAR and GNSS.
Validated trajectories against RTK-GNSS. Measured accuracy, drift and compute cost on an NVIDIA Jetson Xavier NX.
Integrated, extended and evaluated DROID-SLAM, DPVO, ORB-SLAM2/3, stereo SOFT and dense optical-flow VO. This included Jetson (ARM64) builds, ROS 2 wrappers and resource monitoring.

featured.short: ROS 2 robot with YOLO-World open-vocabulary detection, camera–LiDAR fusion and a persistent 3D semantic map.
featured.title: Semantic Robot Perception: Camera–LiDAR Fusion & Semantic Mapping
featured.tagline: A mobile robot that detects objects, places them in 3D and builds a persistent semantic map (ROS 2 Humble + Gazebo).
bullets: Open-vocabulary detection with YOLO-World plus a centroid tracker, so the target classes are set from a config file without retraining.
Camera–LiDAR fusion back-projects each tracked detection through the pinhole model and fuses it with LiDAR range to give a 3D object position.
A semantic map manager registers objects in a database and publishes persistent RViz markers. The pipeline runs as modular ROS 2 packages with custom message interfaces.

publication.title: Vision-Based Odometry: Comparative Analysis on Standard and Custom Datasets for Resource-Limited Vehicle Platforms
publication.authors: N Sai Pranay Kumar, Thippeswamy K S, Dr. Prithvi Sekhar Pagala
publication.abstract: Introduces the Custom GITAM Dataset, a campus-scale visual odometry benchmark recorded on an autonomous ground vehicle with camera, LiDAR and GNSS. The paper compares five monocular VO approaches (feature-based, optical-flow and deep-learning) on KITTI and on this dataset. It measures trajectory accuracy, drift and compute cost on an NVIDIA Jetson Xavier NX, using RTK-GNSS as the reference.
